deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on 'Champs' that lead into the Gr-stacks / globular ∞-groupoid material of Pursuing Stacks. The next page names the category B = (Gr-stacks) with basic objects D_n. The previous page builds globular-type sets F_n out of arrows of categories C_i.

(1) Top line. F = (F_n, s_n, t_n : F_n → F_{n-1}) is a globular set. Grothendieck forms the free abelian groups Z[F_n] with boundary d_n = t_n − s_n, giving a chain complex ... ← Z[F_{n-1}] ← Z[F_n] ← Z[F_{n+1}] ← ... He checks d_{n-1} d_n = 0 on a generator ξ ∈ F_n by computing t_{n-1}(t_nξ − s_nξ) − s_{n-1}(t_nξ − s_nξ). This vanishes by the globular identities s s = s t and t t = t s. This is the naive cellular chain complex of a globular set or ∞-groupoid, i.e. its 'abelianization'.

(2) 'D_n → X'. A map from the standard n-disc (globe) D_n to X is an n-cell, since D_n represents F_n. D_n' is perhaps a variant of the disc, possibly its boundary.

(3) Main content. Let f : F → F' be a morphism of globular sets / ∞-groupoids. Write ∼ for the relation 'related by a higher cell'. Grothendieck gives a staircase of lifting conditions and reads off what each says about homotopy:
- E_0 (a): every s' ∈ F'_0 receives an arrow u : f_0(s) → s' from some f_0(s), with u ∈ F'_1. This is π_0(f) surjective.
- (b): every arrow u' : f_0(s) → f_0(t) in F'_1 has some u : s → t in F_1. This is π_0(f) injective.
- E_1 (b'): the same, but the lift satisfies f(u) ∼ u'. This is π_0 injective and π_1 surjective.
- (c): for parallel u, v ∈ F_1, every w' : f(u) → f(v) in F'_2 has some w : u → v in F_2. This is π_1 injective.
- E_2 (c'): the same with f(w) ∼ w'. This is π_1 injective and π_2 surjective.

The general condition (C_i), in the right column, reads as follows. For every w' ∈ F'_i there is w ∈ F_i with f(w) ∼ w'. Moreover, for i ≥ 1 one may prescribe u = s(w) and v = t(w) in F_{i-1} subject to f(u) = s(w'), f(v) = t(w'). For i ≥ 2 these u, v are parallel: s(u) = s(v), t(u) = t(v). An NB discusses when one can get f(w) = w' exactly.

This is a recursive 'lifting up to higher cells' characterisation of weak equivalences of globular ∞-groupoids: π_n-bijectivity at all base points. It is exactly the shape of the later definition of ω-equivalences of strict ω-categories in the folk model structure, and of weak equivalences of Grothendieck ∞-groupoids.

Purpose: to define weak equivalences in (Gr-stacks) or ∞-groupoids combinatorially, without geometric realisation. The chain complex Z[F] is presumably aimed at homology / linearisation of these objects.
errors: The relation ∼ (f(u) ∼ u' etc.) is used without definition. In the groupoid case it means 'connected by a cell of the next dimension', which is an equivalence relation only thanks to invertibility. For non-groupoidal ω-categories one would need reversible cells.
In (C_i) the text 'f(u)=u', g(v)=v'' is presumably a slip for f(u)=u', f(v)=v' (with u' = s(w'), v' = t(w')).

(C_i) is stated loosely: the existence clause and the 'one may prescribe source/target' clause are run together. The correct formulation is: for all parallel u, v in F_{i-1} and all w' : f(u) → f(v), there exists w : u → v with f(w) ∼ w'.
The identification of (b) and (c) with π_0- and π_1-injectivity implicitly uses groupoid inverses, so that π_1 can be compared at arbitrary base points.
The top chain d = t − s is correct, given the globular identities.

missed.claim: Grothendieck writes down the definition of a weak equivalence of globular ∞-groupoids by stepwise lifting of cells up to a higher cell, with the explicit staircase π_{i-1} injective + π_i surjective. This is formally the definition of ω-equivalence later used by Lafont–Métayer–Worytkiewicz for the folk model structure. If these notes predate 1983, they are an early instance of that definition; but the idea is natural and probably implicit in Pursuing Stacks.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It documents that Grothendieck's own combinatorial notion of weak equivalence for Gr-stacks matches the one used today in ω-category theory and in work on Grothendieck ∞-groupoids (Maltsiniotis, Ara).

deep.surprise_reason: The page cleanly formulates the lifting-up-to-homotopy definition of weak equivalences of globular ∞-groupoids, together with the abelianised chain complex. Both are now standard (folk model structure, Brown–Higgins / Steiner), and the weak-equivalence notion is at least close to Pursuing Stacks. This is a nice prefiguration, but not something a specialist would find unexpected.
